about: Every statewide ballot measure New York voters decided from 1894, the year of the Greater New York consolidation vote, through 2025, with statewide yes and no votes; the 1894 consolidation referendum by county and town; New York City and borough results where the NYC Board of Elections publishes them (2005 to 2025); and New York City charter questions, with results from 2010 on and outcomes for the earlier ones. Greater New York took effect January 1, 1898; its first election was November 2, 1897, and neither 1897 nor 1898 had a statewide measure. 2026 city questions carry the numbers so far from the Board of Elections.

measures.title: Infrastructure maintenance (Ravitch Commission)
src: Report of the New York City Charter Revision Commission, December 1986 to November 1988, Volume One (January 1989), pages 11, 12 and 24: https://www.nyc.gov/assets/charter/downloads/pdf/1986-1988_final_report.pdf

measures.what: City agencies must regularly prepare and update plans for maintaining major capital assets. The Mayor must request the money for that maintenance or explain why not. Passed 88.9% to 11.1%.

measures.label: Proposal 4
measures.title: Administrative reforms (Ravitch Commission)
src: Report of the New York City Charter Revision Commission, December 1986 to November 1988, Volume One (January 1989), pages 11, 12 and 24: https://www.nyc.gov/assets/charter/downloads/pdf/1986-1988_final_report.pdf
https://www.nyc.gov/html/law/downloads/pdf/ar092203.pdf
measures.what: Created the City Administrative Procedure Act: agencies must take public comment when adopting rules, publish the rules and give due process in hearings. Required internal controls for the Mayor and agency heads, and created an independent tribunal for city tax appeals. Passed 85.7% to 14.3%.

measures.label: Proposal 5
measures.title: Succession and filling vacancies (Ravitch Commission)
src: Report of the New York City Charter Revision Commission, December 1986 to November 1988, Volume One (January 1989), pages 11, 12 and 24: https://www.nyc.gov/assets/charter/downloads/pdf/1986-1988_final_report.pdf
https://www.nyc.gov/html/law/downloads/pdf/ar092203.pdf
measures.what: Set a process for deciding when a Mayor is unable to serve. Vacancies for Council Member, Council President, Comptroller and Borough President are filled by voters in special elections, no longer by designees of the Council or Comptroller. Passed 87.2% to 12.8%.

measures.label: Proposal 6
measures.title: Voter assistance and campaign finance (Ravitch Commission)

measures.what: Created a panel to run a nonpartisan program for voter registration and voting. Wrote the Campaign Finance Board into the Charter, including its nonpartisan voter guide, and guaranteed public matching funds for candidates who accept spending and contribution limits. Passed 79.8% to 20.2%.

src: Final Report of the New York City Charter Revision Commission, January 1989 to November 1989 (March 1990), pages 1 and 19 to 21: https://www.nyc.gov/assets/charter/downloads/pdf/1989_final_post-election_report.pdf
https://www.nyc.gov/html/law/downloads/pdf/ar092203.pdf

measures.what: Passed 55% to 45% on November 7, 1989. Eliminated the Board of Estimate and moved its legislative powers to a City Council enlarged to 51 members. Made the Council the final decision-maker on land use in place of the Board, with 50 days to act on a City Planning Commission decision. Gave the Council sole authority to adopt and change the budget. Grew the City Planning Commission to 13 members: seven named by the Mayor, one by each Borough President and one by the Council President. Created Fair Share rules for where the City puts its facilities.
